title: Runaway session allocator isolation and kv-map resync runtime patch
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: Multiple customers (hosted + Dedicated) reported sudden GPU OOM spikes correlated with high short-lived chat sessions and aggressive KV cache prefetching. Investigation found a subtle race between the session allocator's asynchronous compaction and the KV map's tombstone resync logic which could leave GPU allocations pinned (ghost pages) while the KV index believed entries were reclaimed. Under load this caused fragmentation and eventual OOM cascades. This ticket implements a runtime patch: per-tenant allocation generation tagging, an emergency per-tenant token-bucket allocation throttle, and a KV-index resync sweep that runs synchronously during compaction windows. The patch includes feature flags, a canary rollout plan, test harness work, monitoring dashboards, and customer communication artifacts.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start 10k short-lived sessions directed at a quantized model (seq_len 512) across a single GPU pool. 2) Enable aggressive KV prefetch (prefetch_threshold=0.9) and short idle eviction (session_ttl=3s). 3) Observe allocator fragmentation ratio and GPU reserved pages rising until OOMs are triggered. 4) Capture allocator traces and KV index tombstone counts to confirm ghost allocations are present.
root_cause: A mismatch between async allocator compaction and KV index GC: when session teardown raced with KV map tombstone application the allocator sometimes promoted freed slabs into an intermediate state without bumping the allocation generation. Subsequent KV resync logic skipped those slabs believing the keys were gone, leaving pinned GPU pages inaccessible to new allocations and slowly fragmenting available memory until OOMs occurred under bursty traffic.
proposed_fix: 1) Add allocation generation numbers to all session-backed GPU allocations and insist compaction advances and verifies generation before reclaim. 2) Introduce a per-tenant token-bucket throttle that constrains allocation rate during high-churn windows to give compaction time to run. 3) Add a synchronous KV-index resync sweep (configurable window) during compaction that reconciles tombstone state and forces reclamation if stale. 4) Expose emergency 'alloc-throttle' console toggle and automatic fallback to a low-memory-compatible model shard when OOM risk exceeds threshold.
implementation_notes: - New allocator unit tests added for generation semantics. - KV-index sweep implemented as idempotent pass with metrics emitted: kv.resync.sweeps, alloc.generation.mismatches, alloc.throttle.tokens. - Feature gated with runtime flags: alloc_gen_enable, alloc_throttle_enable, kv_sync_sweep_enable. - Backwards compatible: flags default off for older runtime-1.19 nodes; canary is strictly runtime-1.20.
testing_plan: 1) Unit + integration tests exercising generation counter and forced compaction. 2) Synthetic stress harness that mimics customer traffic patterns (short chats, aggressive prefetch). 3) Canary rollout: 5% of hosted traffic in us-west-2 for 24h, then 20% for 48h, then Dedicated opt-in customers. 4) Scale test in internal dedicated environment with 50 tenants concurrent for 12h.
monitoring_and_alerting: Add dashboards and alerts: - Allocator fragmentation ratio > 0.35 (alert P1) - Per-tenant OOM spikes > 3 in 15m (alert P0) - kv.resync.sweeps > 0 with alloc.generation.mismatches > 0 (warning) - alloc_throttle.tokens_depleted (warning). Dashboard links: https://dashboard.redwood.internal/runtime/allocations-ooms and incident timeline: https://dashboard.redwood.internal/incidents/2026-02-12-oom-wave
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flags and land PR (see PR link). 2) Internal canary on staging. 3) 5% hosted canary us-west-2 -> 20% after 24h -> Dedicated opt-in -> full rollout. 4) If anomalies, toggle alloc_throttle_enable=false and revert PR if needed. 5) Post-rollout audit after 7 days.
rollback_plan: Revert PR and disable feature flags. Restore previous autoscaler throttle settings and, if necessary, apply emergency config to reduce KV prefetch aggressiveness. Notify affected customers and schedule next maintenance window for a safer patch.
